title: Late-season low flows showed no clear excess overlap at three Arctic gauges in 31 years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested overlap of low-flow days at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka with ArcticGRO v20261104. We used 31 common complete certified years in 1980-2011. Low flow was below a held-out-year calendar-day 20th percentile. At least two rivers were low on 11.26 August-October days per year, versus an exact independent year-pairing mean of 12.24 days. The difference was -0.99 days; a two-sided conditional permutation test gave p = 0.4648. All six planned checks were also uncertain. This is a same-data extension of earlier spring timing and peak studies to late-season low flows. It does not establish independence, a trend, a cause or coastal freshwater delivery. Short coverage, threshold uncertainty, regulation, source error and conditional exchangeability limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and independent arithmetic checks support reproduction; raw records and record-level derivatives remain external.

display.caption: Observed low-flow overlap and the conditional whole-year pairing reference. The reference distribution is not an effect confidence interval.
